title: Kuulokojeiden sovitus- ja huoltopalvelut ÖVPH Pohjoinen alue
description: Kuulokojeiden sovitus- ja huoltopalvelut ÖVPH Pohjoinen alue Hankinnan kohteena on kuulokojeiden sovitus- ja ylläpitopalvelu Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen pohjoisella osa-alueella. Palveluun sisältyy lääkinnällisenä kuntoutuksena myönnettyjen kuulokojeiden sovitus ja ylläpitopalvelu sekä muiden yksittäisten korvakappaleisiin ja kuulokojeisiin liittyvien huoltotoimenpiteiden hankinta kaudelle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Hankintaan sisältyy kaksi kertaa yhden (1 + 1) vuoden optiomahdollisuus (1.1.2029-31.12.2029 ja 1.1.2030-31.12.2030). Option käyttämisestä tehdään erikseen päätös noin kuusi (6) kuukautta ennen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Toiminta-alue on Pohjoinen alue, johon kuuluu Pietarsaari, Kruunupyy, Luoto, Pedersöre ja Uusikaarlepyy. Pietarsaaren alueella on noin 250 kuulonhuoltoasiakasta per vuosi. Asiakasmäärä on arvio eikä tilaaja sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Palvelun asiakkaalla on oltava palvelua varten korva-, nenä- ja kurkkutautien toimintayksikön toimintaperiaatteiden mukaisesti hyväksytty lähete tai apuvälinepäätös, jonka määräysten mukaan kuulokojepalvelu toteutetaan. Tilaaja varaa oikeuden tarkastella palvelun järjestämistapaa sopimuskauden aikana. Tarkastelun seurauksena palvelun laajuus voi muuttua tai palvelu voidaan osittain tai kokonaan siirtää tilaajan omaksi toiminnaksi hankintasopimuksen ehtojen mukaisesti.,

title: Kohti työtä ja ammattia -kotoutumiskoulutus
description: Kohti työtä ja ammattia -kotoutumiskoulutus Tampereen kaupunki pyytää tarjouksia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kilpailutuksella hankitaan työvoimapalveluiden järjestämisestä annetun lain (380/2023) ja kotoutumisen edistämisestä annetun lain (681/2023) mukaista kotoutumiskoulutusta. Avoimella menettelyllä valitaan yksi palveluntuottaja, jonka kanssa tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa oleva hankintasopimus. Hankittavan palvelun sisältö on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa. Tarjouspyynnön liitteet löytyvät kohdasta Tarjouspyynnön liitteet. Hankittavan palvelun ennakoitu arvo ylittää julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetun lain (hankintalaki 1397/2016) 25 §:n mukaisen kynnysarvon liitteen E hankinnoille, joten kilpailutuksessa sovelletaan hankintalakia. Hankintayksikkö valitsee tarjouksista kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimman. Kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden perusteet (arviointikriteerit) on esitetty tässä tarjouspyynnössä.,

title: Kansallismuseon näyttelykäyttöön tarkoitetut kohdevalaisimet sekä niihin liittyvät vaihdettavat optiikat
description: Kansallismuseon näyttelykäyttöön tarkoitetut kohdevalaisimet sekä niihin liittyvät vaihdettavat optiikat Hankinnan kohteena on Museoviraston / Kansallismuseon ("Hankintayksikkö") museon näyttelykäyttöön tarkoitetut kohdevalaisimet sekä niihin liittyvät vaihdettavat optiikat ja muut tarjouspyynnössä määritellyt lisävarusteet ("Tavara"). Hankittavien tuotteiden määrät ja tekniset vähimmäisvaatimukset on esitetty liitteenä olevassa valaisinluettelossa. Valaisimien tulee olla suoraan mekaanisesti ja sähköisesti yhteensopivia Kansallismuseon olemassa olevien ERCO 3-vaihevalokiskojen kanssa. Valaisimien runkomateriaalin tulee olla alumiinia. Valaisimiin tulee olla saatavana tarjouspyynnössä määritellyt vaihdettavat optiikat sekä värilämpötilaa lämpimämpään ja kylmempään suuntaan muuttavat suodattimet (Cold, Cold Plus, Warm ja Warm Plus tai vastaavat). Tavaralla tulee olla vähintään viiden (5) vuoden tuotetakuu. Takuu- ja huoltopalvelujen tulee olla saatavilla suomen kielellä. Tavara tulee toimittaa 29.1.2027 mennessä. Valituksi tulevan toimittajan tulee pyrkiä toimittamaan Tavara mahdollisimman pian sopimuksen tekemisen jälkeen ja mahdollisuuksien mukaan ennen määräaikaa. Tarkempi aikataulu sovitaan valitun toimittajan kanssa. Aikataulussa on huomioitava, että Tavaran toimitus tapahtuu museon avaamisprojektin aikana. Edellä mainitusta syystä Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden tarjouspyynnössä esitettyjen ajankohtien aikataulumuutoksiin.,

title: Vartiointi- ja turvallisuuspalveluiden hankinta
description: Vartiointi- ja turvallisuuspalveluiden hankinta Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (myöhemmin myös Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia Vartiointi- ja turvallisuuspalveluiden hankintaan. Hankinnan kohteena on koko Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen Vartiointi- ja turvallisuuspalvelut. Hankittavat palvelut jakaantuvat Vartiointi- ja turvallisuuspalveluiden osalta hallinto- ja tukipalveluihin, raportointiin, hälytyskeskuspalveluihin, vartiointiin ja järjestyksenvalvontaan, etävalvontapalveluihin, turvatarkastukseen sekä muihin tarvittaviin turvallisuuspalveluihin. Hankintaan valitaan yksi (1) Toimittaja ja yksi (1) varatoimittaja. Sopimuskausi on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on 12 000 000 euroa. Palvelua tuotetaan pääasiallisesti liitteessä 1.5 Vartiointikohteet -kuvatuissa kohteissa. Liite 1.5 on salassa pidettävä liite ja sitä koskee salassapitosopimus. Mahdollisen tarjoajan tulee toimittaa allekirjoitettu ja pyydetyiltä osin täydennetty sitoumus luottamuksellisena sähköpostina hankinta@luvn.fi osoitteeseen. Salassapitositoumus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä 1.6. Tarkempi kuvaus hankinnan sisällöstä on tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 2. "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus".,

title: Portaiden ja luiskien kaiteet ja käsijohteet, Opintie 2, Kalajoki, Jokilaaksojen koulutuskuntayhtymä
description: Portaiden ja luiskien kaiteet ja käsijohteet, Opintie 2, Kalajoki, Jokilaaksojen koulutuskuntayhtymä Jokilaaksojen koulutuskuntayhtymä kilpailuttaa Kalajoen toimipisteeseen portaiden ja luiskien kaiteet ja käsijohteet asennettuna rakennettavaan päärakennukseen. Toimitusosoite on Opintie 2, 85100 Kalajoki. Hankinta on osa suurempaa pääosin opiskelijatyönä toteutettavaa investointia. Työmaalla työskentelevillä henkilöillä tulee olla VALTTI-kortit ennen työn aloittamista. Tarjouspyyntö sisältää seuraavat kaiteet ja käsijohteet: - Porrashuoneen 102 / 201 kaiteet ja käsijohteet o Suunnitelman ARK 32 Sisäporraspiirustus mukaisesti - Ulkotaso A (pääsisäänkäynti) käsijohteet o Suunnitelman ARK 35 Ulkotasot ja luiskat mukaisesti - Ulkotaso B (valmistuskeittiö) käsijohteet o Suunnitelman ARK 35 Ulkotasot ja luiskat mukaisesti Kaiteiden ja käsijohteiden ominaisuudet ja vaatimukset ovat liitetiedostojen ”ARK 32 Sisäporraspiirustus” ja ”ARK 35 Ulkotasot ja luiskat” mukaiset. Tarjouksen liitteeksi tulee ladata liite, josta selviävät tuotteiden tekniset tiedot tarjouksen oikeellisuuden todentamista varten. Kokonaishinnan tulee sisältää kaiteiden ja käsijohteiden tarkemittauksen, toimituksen sekä asennuksen. Kaiteiden ja käsijohteiden toimittaja suunnittelee kaiteiden kiinnitysdetaljit ja esittää ne tilaajalle. Tilaaja hyväksyy kiinnitysratkaisut ennen kuin kaiteet ja käsijohteet voidaan asentaa. Tarvikkeiden siirrot työkohteeseen kuuluu asennustyöhön. Kaiteiden ja käsijohteiden asennustyön urakoitsija vastaa omien henkilöiden työturvallisuudesta. Toteutusaikataulu: Alustava kaiteiden ja käsijohteiden asennusajankohta on viikko 50/2026. Tarkempi ajankohta sovitaan toimittajan ja tilaajan kesken. Palkkiomuoto ja kulukorvaukset: Tarjous on jätettävä verottomana kokonaishintana (alv 0 %). Hinnan tulee sisältää kaikki työ ja materiaali kustannukset. Maksupostit sovitaan tilauksen yhteydessä. Toimitusosoite on Opintie 2, 85100 Kalajoki. Tarjous tulee jättää kokonaishintana alv 0%. Valintaperusteena kokonaishinnaltaan edullisin tarjous. Laskutuksessa käytetään käännettyä arvonlisäverotusta. Tarjoajan tulee täyttää Tilaajavastuun mukaiset velvoitteet. Hankinnassa sovelletaan YSE1998 sopimusehtoja. Kysymykset tulee esittää Tarjouspalvelun kautta annettuun määräaikaan mennessä, muutoin esitetyt kysymykset ja niihin annetut vastaukset eivät ole hankintayksikköä sitovia. Tarjoukset tulee jättää Tarjouspalvelun kautta, muutoin jätetyt tarjoukset hylätään.,

title: Family Support Services (Inverclyde)
description: Inverclyde Health and Social Care Partnership (HSCP) and the Inverclyde Alcohol and Drug Partnership (ADP) require the delivery of a Family Support Service (FSS) for adults and young people aged 16 years and over, who reside in Inverclyde and are affected by the alcohol and/or drug use of a family member, partner, friend or loved one. The Family Support service will recognise that substance use can have a significant and lasting impact on family members in their own right and that families require support regardless of whether their loved one is currently engaged in treatment, recovery or active substance use. The Family Support service will place families at the centre of all activity and will operate within a framework of: Trauma-Informed Practice Family Inclusive Practice Whole Family Approaches Human Rights Based Practice Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care The Family Support service will provide; early intervention, prevention, emotional support, education, advocacy, peer support, bereavement support, pathways for moving on to other community-based supports when appropriate, and family recovery interventions to improve outcomes for individuals, families and communities across Inverclyde.

description: Inverclyde Health and Social Care Partnership (HSCP) and the Inverclyde Alcohol and Drug Partnership (ADP) require the delivery of a Family Support Service (FSS) for adults and young people aged 16 years and over, who reside in Inverclyde and are affected by the alcohol and/or drug use of a family member, partner, friend or loved one. The Family Support service will recognise that substance use can have a significant and lasting impact on family members in their own right and that families require support regardless of whether their loved one is currently engaged in treatment, recovery or active substance use. The Family Support service will place families at the centre of all activity and will operate within a framework of: Trauma-Informed Practice Family Inclusive Practice Whole Family Approaches Human Rights Based Practice Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care The Family Support service will provide; early intervention, prevention, emotional support, education, advocacy, peer support, bereavement support, pathways for moving on to other community-based supports when appropriate, and family recovery interventions to improve outcomes for individuals, families and communities across Inverclyde.

26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System
description: 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System Solicitation Closes at 02 :00 PM on 26 October 2026 Time Zone EDT RETURN BIDS TO: NRC.BidReceiving-ReceptiondesSoumissions.CNRC@nrc-cnrc.gc.ca Statement of Requirement Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System. The National Research Council of Canada’s (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation (CDI), part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL), requires one (1) integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) to support research, development, testing, method validation, and operational deployments. The system must capture above water topography and shallow water bathymetry within a single factory integrated payload and deliver survey grade outputs through a manufacturer supported hydrographic processing workflow. BACKGROUND: LiDAR is used to generate high accuracy topographic data and digital elevation models by measuring precise distances between a sensor and target surfaces. Conventional topographic LiDAR typically operates at near infrared wavelengths that do not penetrate water, so surveys end at the water surface. To characterize shorelines and other shallow water features within a single survey, a topo bathymetric capability is required to detect both the water surface and submerged bottom under suitable conditions. To support dual use applications such as shoreline mapping, shallow water target detection, wildfire resource assessment, infrastructure inspection, emergency response, and evaluation of potential autonomous landing sites, the Remote Sensing Imaging Group (RSIG) within the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL) requires an integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class RPAS. RSIG, with support from NRC’s Design and Fabrication Department and the Flight Research Laboratory Instrumentation Group, will integrate the system on NRC platforms. Given the field based, survey grade nature of the work, dependable vendor support, training, and documentation are required to maintain operational readiness and minimize downtime, reduce technical risk, and maintain continuity of operations. 1.0 Requirement: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-deployable integrated topographic and bathymetric (topo-bathymetric) LiDAR system (the system), quantity one (1) Specifications: The system must: 1.1 Integrated topo-bathymetric capability -collect both topographic and bathymetric LiDAR data using a single integrated payload 1.2 Bathymetric green laser -use a green laser wavelength (532 nm) providing both terrestrial measurements and water-surface and sub-aqueous bottom returns. 1.3 Unconditional full-waveform recording -record the full return waveform unconditionally for every emitted laser pulse, so that weak submerged-bottom echoes can be recovered, averaged, and reprocessed rather than being permanently lost when they fall below a real-time detection threshold 1.4 Measurement rate and multi-target capability -provide user-selectable measurement rates of up to at least 200 kHz, record at least 15 target returns per emitted pulse, and provide 16-bit intensity information. 1.5 Selectable beam divergence -provide user-selectable laser-beam divergence, adjustable over a range of at least 1 mrad to 6 mrad, so that acquisition can be optimized for different flight altitudes, water clarity, and turbidity conditions. 1.6 Water penetration -be capable of penetrating a minimum of 2 m of clear water under zero-turbidity conditions. 1.7 Scanning field of view - provide an effective scanning field of view of at least 40 degrees perpendicular to the flight direction, equivalent to an off-nadir scan angle of at least 20 degrees, suitable for RPAS topo-bathymetric mapping. 1.8 Integrated survey-grade GNSS/INS - include a fully integrated Global Navigation Satellite System / Inertial Navigation System (GNSS/INS) providing, after post-processing, horizontal position accuracy of 5 cm or better, vertical position accuracy of 10 cm or better, roll and pitch accuracy of 0.02 degrees or better, and heading accuracy of 0.05 degrees or better. The GNSS/INS must be compatible with NRC’s existing Applanix POSPac trajectory post-processing workflow and must be supplied with the required post-processing software licence. 1.9 Integrated RGB camera - include an integrated, co-aligned RGB camera with a minimum resolution of 20 megapixels, supporting co-registration of the LiDAR data with true-colour imagery for draped surface products, structure-from-motion applications, and three-dimensional surface visualization 1.10 Onboard data storage - include internal solid-state data storage and support removable storage media. 1.11 Environmental protection - be suitable for outdoor field operations and provide protection against dust and environmental moisture appropriate for RPAS-based operations, with an ingress protection rating of at least IP64. 1.12 Operating environment - be suitable for operation in Canadian outdoor field conditions, including ambient temperatures below freezing down to -10 °C, and withstand storage and transportation at temperatures down to -20 °C. 1.13 Hydrographic processing software - include manufacturer-supported software covering the complete RPAS-based topo-bathymetric workflow, including: mission planning; system operation and data acquisition; data download and management; inertial data processing; kinematic LiDAR data processing; system calibration; water-surface modelling; correction of underwater measurements for refraction and light-travel time; full-waveform bathymetric analysis; RGB image processing; rigorous data adjustment; quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC); and export of processed data products to commonly used formats, including LAS. 1.14 Calibration - be delivered with system boresight calibration and digital camera calibration completed, together with the applicable calibration documentation for the integrated sensing components. 1.15 Technical Documentation - provide a comprehensive technical manual, including diagrams and/or procedures for troubleshooting and performing basic maintenance tasks. 1.16 RPAS compatibility The complete sensor payload must be suitable for deployment on medium-class RPAS, must have a total payload weight not exceeding 12 kg, and must be capable of integration on NRC’s medium-class RPAS through appropriate mechanical, electrical, and communications interfaces, and must operate from a DC power supply of 18–34 VDC. 1.17 Manufacturer repairs All repairs and recalibration must be performed at the manufacturer’s facility or by a manufacturer-authorized service provider, with documentation provided following each repair or recalibration. 2.0 Training: The Contractor must provide comprehensive RPAS-based topo-bathymetric operations and workflow training for up to four (4) NRC personnel covering, at minimum: • mission planning; • system operation and data acquisition; • operational best practices; • data download; • inertial data processing; • refraction correction; • LiDAR and image data processing; • full-waveform bathymetric analysis; • data quality assurance and • quality control (QA/QC); and export of processed data products. The location of the training to be determined following integration of the system on an NRC RPAS. 3.0 Warranty and Support: 3.1 Warranty The system and all supplied hardware must include a minimum twelve (12) month manufacturer’s warranty covering material and manufacturing defects and operation within the manufacturer’s specifications, commencing upon acceptance of the goods. The warranty must include access to interim software releases and version updates issued during the warranty period. title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Parksville, Qualicum, Comox Valley
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) Solicitation #: 30008200 This requirement is for Fisheries and Oceans Canada Title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Parksville, Qualicum, Comox Valley Objective: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, requires Contractors to provide delivery and coordination services for the Stream to Sea Program, as defined by the Project Authority, for schools within School Districts listed below, as well as Independent Schools, other Learning Centres, and community partners in the same geographic area: Parksville, Qualicum, Comox Valley (including School Districts (SD) 69 and 71) Stream to Sea Program delivery and coordination services are required over the entire duration of this Contract with some times requiring more commitment than others. Delivery and coordination services will be defined on a geographic specific basis through the development of work plan details using the information provided in Appendix 1 (Statement of Work). The Contractor will work with the Project Authority, to coordinate and deliver the Stream to Sea Program in schools and with local community groups. The work will consist of training educators, coordinating and assisting with set up of classroom incubators (aquaria), delivering salmon eggs to schools, providing classroom (indoor and outdoor) sessions which may include the salmon life cycle, fish dissections, aquatic ecosystems and habitat requirements for salmon, environmental sustainability as it relates to salmon, stream to sea migration and other salmon focused education pertinent to the area. The Contractor will provide trouble shooting and maintenance support for aquaria in schools and develop or assist with the development and delivery of a spring fry release program for participating schools. In some instances, the Contractor may participate in the live transport of adult and juvenile salmon and may participate in the spawning of broodstock. Contractor will also support Pacific Region tracking and reporting (i.e. brood stock summary and year end stream to sea data collection/reporting). The Stream to Sea Program aims to develop opportunities for external parties to be involved. Contractors may be required to facilitate and develop opportunities with local communities, First Nations, and community groups. Security Requirement: There is no security associated with this requirement. Period of Contract: The period of contract shall be from date of award to October 31, 2027. There are two (2) option periods of one (1) year to be exercised at the discretion of the Department. Trade Agreements: The requirement is subject to the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). title: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Hissien huolto- ja korjauspalvelut
description: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Hissien huolto- ja korjauspalvelut HANKINNAN KOHDE Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjoustanne hallinnoimiensa kiinteistöjen hissien huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sekä hälytyskeskuspalveluista. Hankinnan kohteena ovat hissien kokonaisvaltainen huolto-, kunnossapito-, korjaus- ja päivystyspalvelu. Palveluun sisältyvät lisäksi hissien toiminnan ylläpitämiseksi tarvittavat muut huolto- ja korjaustoimenpiteet. Palvelun tavoitteena on varmistaa hissien turvallinen, luotettava ja keskeytyksetön toiminta sekä ylläpitää laitteiden tekninen kunto valmistajien ohjeiden, viranomaismääräysten ja hyvän kunnossapitotavan mukaisesti. Hankinnan tarkempi sisältö on kuvattu tämän tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 (Palvelunkuvaus). Lisäksi liitteessä 2, (Laiteluettelo / Tarjousliite) on kerrottu jokaisen hissin vaadittu huoltomäärä vuodessa. SOPIMUSJÄRJESTELY Hankinnasta muodostetaan puitejärjestely yhden (1) palveluntuottajan kanssa. TOIMEKSIANTOJEN TOTEUTUS Perushuollot toteutetaan sovitun huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti. Kiireettömien töiden tilaukset tehdään P2P-tilausjärjestelmällä, joka toimii samalla tilauksen sopimuksena. Tilauksen yhteydessä sovitaan toimeksiannon sisältö, aikataulu sekä arvioitu työmäärä. Mikäli sovitusta aikataulusta myöhästytään palveluntuottajasta johtuvasta syystä, tilaajalla on oikeus periä sopimusluonnoksen mukaiset sanktiot. HINNOITTELU JA TARJOUKSEN SISÄLTÖ Tarjous tulee laatia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Tarjouksen tulee kattaa kaikki palvelun toteuttamiseksi tarvittavat työt. Mahdolliset lisätyöt hinnoitellaan tarjouspyynnön mukaisesti. Perushuollot laskutetaan laitekohtaisilla tarjoushinnoilla. Muut huolto- ja korjaustyöt laskutetaan tarjotun tuntihinnan sekä toteutuneen materiaalikulutuksen mukaisesti. SOPIMUSKAUSI Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta. Sopimuskauden tavoiteltu alkamispäivä on 1.12.2026. Mikäli sopimuskauden aloitus viivästyy esimerkiksi muutoksenhaun vuoksi, sopimuskausi alkaa vasta, kun asiaan on saatu lainvoimainen ratkaisu. Määräaikaisen sopimuskauden jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa optioilla: - yksi (1) + yksi (1) vuotta Optiokaudet alkavat tavoitellusti: - 1.11.2028 (1. optiovuosi) - 1.11.2029 (2. optiovuosi) Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä. Sopimus jatkuu optiokausille automaattisesti, ellei tilaaja ilmoita kirjallisesti halustaan olla käyttämättä optiota viimeistään kuusi (6) kuukautta ennen kunkin optiokauden alkamista. HISSIEN LISÄÄMINEN JA POISTAMINEN Sopimuskaudella hankinnan kohteet voivat lisääntyä tai vähentyä ja tilaajalla on oikeus lisätä tai poistaa kohteita sopimuksesta ilman irtisanomisaikaa. Lisättyihin ja poistettuihin kohteisiin sovelletaan tarjouksen mukaisia hintatasoja. TAKUUAIKAISTEN HISSIEN HUOLTOVASTUU Tämä hankinta ei koske takuuaikaisia huolto- ja korjauspalveluja. Takuuaikaiset hissit pysyvät toimituksesta tai hissin korjauksesta vastanneen toimittajan huollossa takuuajan päättymiseen saakka. Takuuajan päätyttyä huolto- ja korjausvastuu siirtyy tämän sopimuksen mukaiselle palveluntuottajalle. Tilaaja ilmoittaa palveluntuottajalle takuuajan päättymisajankohdan. SOPIMUSEHDOT JA HANKINTAPÄÄTÖS Palvelussa noudatetaan JYSE 2025 -ehtoja. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää tarjoajan omia ehtoja. HANKINNAN KÄYTTÄJÄT Sopimusta voivat käyttää Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitoksen lisäksi myös muut Oulun kaupungin hallintokunnat ja liikelaitokset, joilla on sama Y-tunnus, kuten Oulun Kaupunkiympäristöpalvelut ja Oulun Vesi.,

title: Biometric Identity Services
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as an obligation on the part of the Government. This is NOT a Request for Quotations or Proposals. No solicitation document exists, and a formal solicitation may or may not be issued by the Government as a result of the responses received to this RFI. The Government will not pay for any response or demonstration expenses. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback concerning their submission. All submissions will become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Responding to the RFI is completely voluntary and will not enhance or adversely affect responses to any resulting solicitation if such solicitation is issued at a later date. There is no competitive advantage gained by any of the respondents to this RFI. DESCRIPTION The Office of Biometric Identity Management (OBIM) is the Congressionally designated lead entity within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), responsible for biometric identity services. The capability to match, store, share, and analyze biometric identity information includes OBIM�s operation, maintenance, and improvement of the central DHS biometric repository which is currently the Automated Biometric Identification System (IDENT), and in the future the in-development replacement system for IDENT, Homeland Advanced Recognition Technology (HART). OBIM provides DHS and its mission partners with biometric identity services that enable national security and public safety decision making. As one of the world�s largest biometric repositories, OBIM�s biometric system contains the identities of over 300 million individuals. OBIM Identity Operations Division (IOD) is seeking professional services to provide biometric examiners, multimodal biometric examiners and identity services to support OBIM with multimodal biometric accuracy and identity services expertise for the Biometric Accuracy Analysis Team (BAAT) and Biometric Support Center (BSC), to support OBIM�s current and future biometric capabilities. OBIM�s biometric system currently utilizes fingerprints, latent prints, face, and iris to support its biometric mission needs but expects the capabilities to expand to meet stakeholder needs in the future. The contractor shall provide multimodal biometric accuracy and identity services expertise to include: � Biometric examination services � Identity management capabilities and biometric support services � Biometric accuracy and quality analysis � Data analysis Government provided software will be used in support of this work effort. Software used may change during the course of the contract; however, the type of work will remain the same. The contractor shall provide multimodal biometric accuracy and identity services expertise to include: Biometric examination services for all modalities Identity management capabilities and biometric support services Biometric accuracy and quality analysis Data analysis In addition, as part of this effort, the Government expects: Innovative approaches to staffing in order to ensure resources are applied in the most efficient manner Application of industry best practices across all tasks Collaboration across BAAT and BSC teams to ensure mission needs are met and opportunities for efficiency improvements are identified The contractor is responsible for providing oversight of the work performed in accordance with the Project Management Plan and for establishing/maintaining a Quality Assurance program. Biometric Examiner and Identity Management Services Although OBIM�s biometric system is very accurate and executes hundreds of thousands of biometric services each day, BSC biometric examiners and analysts are needed to supplement the automated capabilities of the system, respond to stakeholder requests for biometrics identity services, and to maintain and improve the accuracy of the system through identity management tasks and in support of the BAAT accuracy activities. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel to support the Biometric Support Center (BSC) with the following duties: Analyze and compare biometric images to render identity decisions when the automated matchers are unable Resolve candidate lists generated by the automated system when biometrics are searched Prepare reports as needed to support examiner identity decision conclusions Correct biometric capture issues so that future matching is improved Maintain the identities within IDENT/HART through record reviews and analysis of biometric identity conflicts, errors, etc. Support stakeholder biometric service requests for those stakeholders who are not able to execute these requests through automated capabilities Provide subject matter expertise and technical support in support of BSC operations Note: The BSC is not a forensic laboratory; therefore, the scope of this work does not include the handling/processing of physical evidence. Biometric Accuracy and Data Analysis Additionally, the contractor shall provide data accuracy and quality analysis to manage the accuracy of biometric identity information. The government is expecting support for the Biometric Accuracy Analysis Team (BAAT) which is dedicated to the monitoring, analysis, reporting, and correction of the biometric data within the HART database. The contractor is responsible for providing data integrity analysis, reporting services and related analysis services, as required, for OBIM�s IOD. Support includes technical subject matter expertise, project management services as well as audit recommendations and advice on corrective actions and guidance to the field. The contractor shall also provide statistical analysis of system data to support requirements identification. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel to support the Biometric Accuracy Analysis Team (BAAT) with the following duties: Conducting comprehensive testing of biometric data to assess accuracy and quality of stakeholder biometric data, vendor matchers, presentation attack detection tools, and data quality software Supporting the development, implementation and automation of biometric programs Collaborate within OBIM and with stakeholders to ensure alignment with operational goals and standards to improve biometric match response accuracy Create statistically representative biometric data cohorts as authorized to support mission needs Perform ad hoc root-cause-analysis of biometric based anomalies. Enhance existing processes, infrastructure, and architecture to better support operations Support the maintenance and production of Microsoft Power Platform based applications Ensure adherence to record keeping protocols by leveraging existing methods and applying authorized process improvements methods Publish impactful findings to support best practices throughout OBIM and its stakeholders Attend conferences and meetings related to biometric knowledge sharing to support OBIM Establish metrics to enable a notification-based dashboard to support system monitoring Task Order Management The government expects: The establishment and maintenance of a roadmap that aligns the efforts of the BSC and BAAT with the broader Systems Business Operations Branch. The design, development, and integration of Microsoft Power Platform solutions, existing Excel reports, and the Pyramid Business Intelligence application to seamlessly dashboard key performance metrics. Routine coordination and planning between Key Personnel; Biometric Examiner Lead and Biometric Information Technology/Identification Systems Specialist to establish seamless methods of documenting, tracking, reporting, and supporting contractor activity. Tilaajat hankkivat pääosin vuokrattavia laitteita, ja vähäisissä määrin laitteita tullaan ostamaan omaksi. Ilmanpuhdistimilla haetaan väliaikaista ratkaisua sisäilmaongelmien hallintaan käyttöä turvaavana toimenpiteenä. Ilmanpuhdistimien tulee olla tarkoitettu tähän käyttötarkoitukseen. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Kilpailutus suoritetaan avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella jokaiseen osa-alueeseen puitetoimittajiksi valitaan kolme (3) vertailussa eniten pisteitä saanutta tarjoajaa etusijajärjestyksessä. Hankinta kilpailutetaan yhteishankintana niin, että Vantaan kaupunki julkaisee tarjouspyynnön. Kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään samansisältöiset, sopimusluonnoksen (liite 1) mukaiset sopimukset Vantaan kaupungille, Kauniaisten kaupungille ja Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman päätöksensä. Vantaan kaupungille tehtävien sopimusten perusteella hankintoja voivat tehdä Vantaan kaupungin kaikki toimialat sekä Vantaan Tilapalvelut Vantti Oy, VTK Kiinteistöt Oy- konserni, VAV Yhtymä Oy, VAV Asunnot Oy, VAV Palvelukodit Oy, VAV Hoiva-asunnot Oy, Hakopolun Liikekiinteistö Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Hakucenter, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Maakotkantie 10, Pallastunturintien Liikekiinteistö Oy ja Asunto Oy Vantaan Katriinanrinne. Sopimustoimittaja voi tarjota samoin ehdoin tuotteitaan ja palvelujaan Vantaan kaupungin seuraaville konsernitoimijoille: Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ja Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Sote-tilat. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella (2) yhden (1) vuoden optiolla (1+1). Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa ilmoitettuihin euromääräisiin arvoihin tai tiettyihin arvioituihin hankintamääriin sopimuskaudella., Osa-alue 1: Puhtaanilmantuotto 160 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistuslaitteiden vuokraus ja hankinta toimistotiloihin., Osa-alue 2: Puhtaanilmantuotto 400 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistinten vuokraus ja hankinta., Osa-alue 3: Puhtaanilmantuotto 800 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistinten vuokraus ja hankinta isoihin tiloihin.,

title: Valentinlyst helse- og velferdssenter - optimalisering av ansatteareal
description: Trondheim eiendom inviterer til åpen anbudskonkurranse for prosjektet Valentinlyst HVS - optimalingsering av brukerareal.Bakgrunnen for prosjektet er endret bruk og økt bemanning på senteret. Det ble derfor satt i gang et mulighetsstudie i 2025, for å se på optimalisering av ansattarealene for alle enhetene som er lokalisert på sentret. Behovet er mer garderobeplass og flere møte- og kontorfasiliteter.Ombyggingsprosjektet omfatter etablering av flere og større garderober i kjeller, mindre ombygginger av eksisterende kontor og møterom for å dekke dagens behov, samt sørge for at medisinrom overholder dagens krav.Omfanget på arealet er ca. 900m2.Prosjektet gjennomføres etter NS 8405.

title: Debris Boom Supply and Install at Harry S. Truman Lake Project
description: The purpose of the debris boom is to prevent floating debris from impacting the dam's tainter gates, which is crucial for maintaining the full operational capacity of the spillway. The boom will also serve as a visual barrier to boaters. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, engineering, fabrication, delivery, and optional installation necessary to furnish a complete debris boom system at Harry S. Truman Dam. The approximately 2,000-foot boom shall be designed to intercept floating debris upstream of the spillway and withstand site-specific hydraulic, wind, wave, debris, and impact loading conditions. The debris boom shall be designed for an 800-foot-long by 3-foot-thick debris field, use a minimum safety factor of 2.0 for design loads, withstand a direct head-on impact from an 18-inch-diameter, 100-foot-long log traveling at the maximum design water velocity, and withstand design conditions including 50 mph wind speed and 5-foot wave height. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns and is competed as full and open competition, Unrestricted. An organized site visit has been scheduled for: Friday, 9 October 2026 at 11am.

title: Heating, Ventilation, Plumbing Maintenance Services, various locations, Nunavut
description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Arviat, Baker Lake, Chesterfield Inlet, Coral Harbour, Naujaat, Rankin Inlet, and Whale Cove, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for preventative maintenance and inspection services for heating systems, including oil-fired boilers, furnaces, and domestic hot water heaters, to ensure their safe, reliable, and efficient operation at the RCMP Arviat Detachment, Baker Lake Detachment, Chesterfield Inlet Detachment, Coral Harbour Detachment, Naujaat Detachment, Rankin Inlet Detachment and Whale Cove Detachment. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 3 Years from the date of contract. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, and 70% for price. Bidders may submit bids for any location. Bids will be evaluated separately for each location. As a result, multiple contracts may be awarded. Based on the number of locations (7), up to seven (7) contracts may be issued. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

description: The National Trust is seeking a suitably qualified contractor to deliver woodland creation, hedgerow planting, fencing, and associated landscape improvement works at Skernaghan Point, Islandmagee, County Antrim. This project forms part of the National Trust's wider habitat restoration and nature recovery programme, aimed at enhancing biodiversity, improving habitat connectivity, and increasing climate resilience within this important coastal landscape. The successful contractor will be responsible for the provision of all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision, and management required to complete the works. Key elements of the contract include: • Native woodland creation within designated planting areas. • Establishment of native mixed-species hedgerows. • Supply and installation of stock-proof fencing. • Installation of gates, access infrastructure, and drinking troughs where specified. • Ground preparation, vegetation management, and ancillary establishment works. • Supply and installation of six timber dams (approximately 3m wide using larch rounds), with locations to be confirmed during the site visit. All works must be completed in accordance with National Trust requirements, project specifications, and industry best practice. Contractors are invited to submit a fixed-price quotation for the delivery of the works." Date of Issue; 05/10/26 Clarification Deadline: 19/10/26 RFP Return Deadline: 26/10/26 This opportunity is being conducted on the Proactis Plaza portal. https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/ Click on the "Opportunities" button and filter on Customer name - The National Trust All communication is to be carried out via the Proactis portal.

title: CONTRACTOR-OPERATED PARTS STORE (COPARS)
description: To provide repair parts, replacement components, supplies, materials, equipment and services in support of automotive, forklift, heavy equipment, material handling, construction, and civil engineering equipment maintenance, via a staffed on-site parts store or contractor-owned consignment inventory, on-demand delivery service, or a combination of two or more methods. This effort supports the United States Marine Corps (USMC) Southwest Region Fleet Transportation (SWRFT) division, which consist of seven (7) sites throughout California and Arizona. SWRFT is responsible for the management, readiness, and operational support of vehicles and equipment that support Marine Corps installation commanders and tenant activities located in the Southwestern United States. The SWRFT consists of Southern California Region sites at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Camp Pendleton, CA; Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar, CA; Marine Corps Recruit Depot (MCRD) San Diego, CA; Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC), Twentynine Palms, CA; Marine Corps Logistics Base (MCLB) Barstow, CA; and Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center (MCMWTC) Bridgeport, CA; as well as Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Yuma, AZ located outside the Southern California region.

title: Mosquito Lake Control Tower Structural Standing Seam Metal Roof Replacement
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District has a project that involves the complete replacement of the standing seam metal roof on the Control Tower Building at Mosquito Creek Lake in Cortland, Ohio. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). Rough Estimate of this non-commercial construction project is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The work includes rerouting existing vent and exhaust pipes through the masonry side wall, installing a new gutter system, and integrating a new, certified, non-penetrating Lightning Protection System. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 238160 - Roofing Contractors. The Small Business Size Standard is $19,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Contract. The Request for Quote (RFQ) will be issued on, or about, 4 September 2026, via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov. The anticipated award date is 13 November 2026. Basis of Award is best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO 12.203(a), price and past performance. title: DUAL ENROLLMENT PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is seeking capability statements from eligible Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) interested in establishing no-cost Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) or Memorandums of Agreement (MOAs) to support dual or concurrent enrollment opportunities for DoWEA students worldwide. This announcement seeks institutional, academic, financial, technical, cybersecurity, privacy, and programmatic information from IHEs to assess their capability to participate in a dual enrollment partnership program pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2164c. This announcement is not a solicitation for proposals, request for quotations, request for offers, grant opportunity, or procurement action, and no contract award is contemplated. Responses will be used solely to evaluate institutional capabilities and determine whether DoWEA may pursue discussions regarding one or more no-cost MOUs or MOAs. Submission of a response does not guarantee selection, discussions, execution of an agreement, student participation, enrollment volumes, or future opportunities. Any resulting MOU or MOA will be non-procurement in nature and will not obligate the Government to expend funds, pay tuition or fees, reimburse participants, refer students, guarantee enrollments, or enter into any agreement. DoWEA may select one, multiple, or no respondents and reserves the right to discontinue consideration of any response at any time. All interested IHEs should review the full announcement for eligibility requirements, submission instructions, and response deadlines. For more information, please see attachment 27R0001_DualEnroll_OA_092426

title: Request for Information Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense Avenger Weapon System Support
description: Request for Information Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense Avenger Weapon System Support Synopsis: The Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense (SHIELD) Project Office is conducting market research to determine if there are potential sources with the capability to provide engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201 (e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. The Government Point of Contact will be Ms. Lillian Irby, U.S. Army Contracting Command-Redstone, and can be contacted via email: lillian.m.irby.civ@army.mil. EMAIL ONLY, NO PHONE CALLS. Administrative: In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. Per FAR 52.215-3, Request for Information (RFI) or Solicitation for Planning Purposes: a. The U.S. Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information solicited, except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the FAR. b. Although the term �proposal� may be used in this RFI, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. c. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and should not be considered as a request for proposals or as a solicitation to do business with the U.S. Government. Avenger System Overview: The Avenger mission is to provide a lightweight, highly mobile, shoot-on-the-move, day/night, short-range surface-to-air missile and gun weapon system. Mounted on an M1097A2 High Mobility Multi-Purpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV), it engages Fixed Wing, Rotary Wing, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, and Cruise Missile threats. The Avenger M47A2 derivative system, termed Slew-to-Cue, receives cues to a track from an outside source and automatically slews to and follows the target beyond the line of sight. Avenger System Description: The Avenger Weapon System is a critical component of the Army�s Short Range Air Defense System (SHORADS). The system consists of: Two Standard Vehicle Mounted Launchers mounted on a turret A .50 caliber machinegun Forward Looking Infrared Laser Range Finder Environmental Control Unit/Prime Power Unit Auto-track systems and Identification Friend or Foe system Two 12V, 100 AMP lead-acid batteries connected in series (24V system power) 360 degrees continuously rotating, gyro-stabilized turret mounted on the HMMWV The fire unit can engage targets with missiles or the machinegun while on-the-move or stationery. The gunner can operate the system in-turret or from a remote location using the Remote-Control Unit. Scope of Work and Contractor Requirements: The SHIELD Project Office is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System and all derivative systems. Note: Proposers must have the required capability at the start of the performance period and must be able to perform all required tasks. Partial solution proposals will not be considered. Core Support Areas: The contractor will be responsible for complex system engineering, manufacturing, test equipment, logistics, and sustainment support. Support includes, but is not limited to: Engineering and Integration: Providing detailed technical expertise for Avenger Weapon Systems, Line Replaceable Units (LRU) (all variants), support equipment, and system interfaces. Designing and fabricating new solutions based on the current Avenger design to meet U.S. Government requirements. Performing complex system integration tasks. Providing software engineering and development for current and future software requirements. Providing in-depth system engineering analysis to support performance improvement, failure analysis, and other engineering activities. Testing & Analysis: Supporting test activities, including the assessment of test results. Providing design and technical support for existing and future contractor- and U.S. Government-owned test equipment. Performing reliability assessments and failure analysis with corrective action identification at the system and LRU level. Quickly and effectively analyzing and resolving hardware/software failures to restore operational capability. Logistics: Performing logistics functions, including technical manual generation/modification, maintenance support, system repairs and Field Service Representative support. Training and Fielding: Redesigning, replacing, installing, and training on all LRUs. Conducting training and system deployment, including New Equipment Training. Supporting sustainment training for deployed systems. Quality Assurance and Security: Complying with all Quality Assurance requirements (configuration management). Maintaining a facility compliant with all federal, state, and local requirements. Ensuring compliance with current DoW Information Assurance and Cybersecurity requirements. Meeting all contractor security, Communications Security, Federal, and DoW requirements, including Defense Security Service accreditation for both unclassified and classified information. Personnel Requirements: The U.S. Government requires a team of Field Service Representatives with expertise in Weapon Systems operation, sustainment, mechanical/electrical maintenance, physical security, and site maintenance. Security Clearance: Contractor employees will be required to hold and maintain a Secret security clearance. Operations: The contractor is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation and maintenance of Avenger Weapon Systems and sites. Provide a statement describing your company as domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate country of ownership). Part B. Past Experience: Describe up to five previous projects similar in complexity to this requirement. Include contract numbers, a brief description of work, period of performance, supported agency/organization, and individual points of contact (Contracting Officer or Program Manager). Defense Systems and Avenger Experience: What experience do you have planning and executing the deployment and sustainment of weapons/defense systems? The purpose of this notice is strictly to conduct market research to determine the availability and capability of Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs), and other responsible sources capable of performing the requirement described herein. Responses will be used to assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including the applicability of the Buy Indian Act (25 U.S.C. 47) and HHSAR Subpart 326.6, Acquisitions Under the Buy Indian Act. title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Contractor to fabricate awards; certificates and medallions
description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Contractor to fabricate awards; certificates and medallions
description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. title: Sources Sought / Request for Information � BENEFEDS Federal Benefits Enrollment and Premium Administration Services (Follow-On)
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. It is not a solicitation, does not constitute a commitment by the Government, and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Responses will not be reimbursed. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is conducting market research for the follow-on acquisition of BENEFEDS, the Government-sponsored enrollment, premium and allotment administration, and customer service platform supporting the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP), the Federal Flexible Spending Account Program (FSAFEDS), and the Federal Long Term Care Insurance Program (FLTCIP). The anticipated requirement includes FEDVIP enrollment and eligibility services; premium and payroll-allotment administration across more than fifty payroll and annuity providers; a bilingual multi-channel contact center; education, communications, and Open Season support; the information systems, security authorization, privacy, accessibility, and continuity functions that underpin the services; reporting; fraud, waste, and abuse prevention; and transition-in and transition-out. The current contract, IDIQ 24322622D0006, was competitively awarded June 28, 2022; services for calendar year 2027 are being provided under a task order on that contract. OPM anticipates award of the follow-on in spring 2027 with full services beginning on or about December 31, 2027. OPM seeks (1) capability and business-size information from firms of all sizes, including small businesses in every socioeconomic category, to support its small business determination, and (2) industry comments on the anticipated requirement, the draft performance standards, the transition approach, and the contract structure � including anything OPM has not listed that a capable benefits administrator would expect to see specified. The attached notice describes the requirement and the information requested; Attachment 1 is the required response format. Questions about this notice are due by 3:00 p.m. ET, Wednesday, October 14, 2026, by email to James.Faulkner@opm.gov and Dennis.Hodges@opm.gov. Responses are due by 3:00 p.m. ET, Monday, October 26, 2026, by email to both addresses with the subject line "BENEFEDS SSN/RFI Response � [Company Name]". OPM may invite selected respondents to 30-minute virtual sessions during the week of November 2, 2026. All communication is through the two points of contact above; do not contact other OPM personnel.

title: Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic
description: N0016426SNBXX REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) PSC J052, J066, H266, H366 NAICS 541380, 811219 1.0 Objective & Background This Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought (SS) notice is issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division Contracting Department, Crane, IN. The NSWC Crane Contracting Department is conducting market research to identify potential industry partners capable of providing comprehensive calibration services in accordance with OPNAV 3960.16 for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE). Currently, NSWC Crane utilizes organic support in combination with a SeaPort Task Order and a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for calibration of TMDE for navy programs at NSWC Crane. The Government is exploring the feasibility of consolidating these requirements into a single, multi-year contract (e.g., Base Year plus Option Years). The primary objective of this market research is to determine if industry is interested in running the calibration program in accordance with the OPNAV 3960.16 at the contractor's own facility or government owned contractor ran facility. The Government is seeking capability statements regarding the calibration of approximately 2,700 unique TMDE types and ~7,000 total TMDE assets annually to ensure operational readiness and strict compliance with technical standards. 2.0 Acquisition Strategy & Disclaimer THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Navy has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Information gathered from this market research will directly inform the Government's future acquisition strategy, including the determination of contract type, the feasibility of consolidating these calibration services, and the viability of shifting the primary place of performance to contractor-owned facilities. 3.0 Incumbent Contract Information The current workload is distributed across the following contract vehicles: Supported Equipment N0017819D8285/N0016423F3007 Goldbelt ILS 5/1/2023-4/30/2028 Unsupported Equipment N0016426A0026 Cross technologies 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0025 ENI 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0024 Transcat 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0023 Micro precision 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0022 Tektronix 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 4.0 Summary of Requirements The required calibration services span multiple asset categories. All calibration services must be performed in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025, navy approved and/or specialized approved procedures. Technical Standard & Location Requirements: The Government intends for the bulk of calibration services to be performed by the contractor at the contractor's facility. All calibrations must conform strictly to the ISO/IEC 17025 standard. While most calibration efforts will be conducted at contractor facilities and on station at NSWC Crane, there will be a significant amount of calibration workload that will be conducted at various industry locations supporting NSWC Crane workload. Locations vary across Indiana and adjoining states and are subject to change through the life of the contract. Logistics requirements: Personnel physically inspect the shipping container and the TMDE itself for transit damage. Onsite Pick up/delivery of assets 2-5 times per week Reference MIL-STD-2073-1 for assets over $10,000 Verifies that all components listed on the shipper's DD Form 1149 or stowage list are present. Engineering services: The Contractor shall provide high level support in Metrology and Calibration Laboratory for various project and programs at NSWC CRANE. Various Administration support: Contractors must maintain rigorous, auditable stewardship of all GFP throughout its lifecycle using the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) GFP Module. Workload Distribution The historical and projected annual workload includes, but is not limited to, the following functional shop code categories: Shop Code Category Estimated Annual Calibration Volume TORQUE - 1,219 METERS/D&A - 1,070 POWER SUPPLIES - 571 FIELD CAL (Onsite) - 341 HANDTOOLS - 275 PRESSURE/VACUUM - 175 MICROWAVE ACTIVE - 394 SIG GEN - 276 TEMP/HUMIDITY - 454 Other Specialized Equipment - ~2,000+ (Combined) 5.0 Submission Instructions Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a comprehensive capability statement addressing their ability to meet the workload requirements outlined in Section 4.0. Responses are due no later than 1400 EST on 26 October 2026 Submission Format Requirements Page Limit Responses shall be limited to 5 pages. Delivery Method Submissions must be sent via e-mail only to the designated Point of Contact. Proprietary Info Must be minimized and clearly marked. Please segregate proprietary information to aid the Government's review. Required Information to Include Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement addressing the following key areas: Corporate Overview Company name, CAGE code, UEI, socio-economic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), SDVOSB), and current CMMC Certification Level. Contractor Facility Capacity Explicit confirmation of the vendor's ability to host and process this volume of equipment at their own facility, rather than relying on Government space. The contractor should be within distance capable of being here 2-5 a week. Technical Capability Overview of laboratory capabilities for the listed categories, current accreditations (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540.1, ANSI/NCSL Z540.3), and capacity to maintain industry standard turnaround times (TAT) for high-volume throughput. Logistics and Handling Specific processes for managing the logistics pipeline: secure transportation, shipping/receiving of government assets, and the methodology for dispatching technicians for the ~340 required onsite (field) calibrations. Government Points of Contact Direct all questions regarding this RFI and submit all capability statements to the following designated point of contact: Primary POC: Andrew Figg andrew.n.figg.civ@us.navy.mil Secondary POC Anthony Morin anthony.m.morin5.civ@us.navy.mil 6.0 Attachments OPNAVINST 3960.16C List of Unique TMDE (Excel File)
