title: CAAA Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) BOA
description: SECTION A � SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure the Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) supply requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 332710 (Machine Shops; Size Standard: 500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 0001 - RASP BOA Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 5340 (Hardware, Commercial). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a RASP BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future RASP orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) operations across the categories defined in Section B. Items ordered may include detailed specifications from controlled technical data packages referencing military specifications (MIL-SPEC) or restricted technical drawings. 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussions. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) The following unfunded CLINs are established at the master agreement level for administrative categorization only: CLIN 0001: Machined and Fabricated Metal Parts (NAICS 332710 / 332999) CLIN 0002: Plastics and Injection Molded Components (NAICS 326199) CLIN 0003: Wooden Containers, Boxes, and Pallets (NAICS 321920) CLIN 0004: Chemicals, Organic and Inorganic (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0005: Paints, Coatings, and Adhesives (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0006: Miscellaneous Hardware, Tools, and Gaskets (NAICS 332510) CLIN 0007: Other Class IX Sustainment Products SECTION C � CAAA RASP EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES A BOA is not a contract (FAR 16.703(a)). An order becomes a binding contract upon Government acceptance and award. The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) supply category listed in Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description by completing Attachment 0004 � Combined Technical and Past Performance Questionnaire. No site visits are required at this stage. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order RFQ. Detail PDs, TDPs, and QA requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. ALIGNMENT All supplies delivered under individual orders must support manufacturing and readiness at CAAA. Processes, tolerances, and quality controls must align with technical data packages (TDPs) provided at the order level. 2. JOINT CERTIFICAITON PROGRAM (JCP) Master BOA Level: To be eligible for a master BOA, and to maintain eligibility, the contractor must possess and maintain active JCP registration to access export-controlled TDPs and drawings. Verification: The Government will independently verify JCP status prior to execution. Failure to maintain active certification results in immediate termination of the BOA. Subcontractors: Prime contractors must ensure subcontractors are registered in the JCP if they require access to restricted drawings. Information Link: Procedures are available at the DLA Joint Certification Program (JCP) Website. 3. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the RASP BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 52.219-33): Non-manufacturers must supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer, unless an SBA class or individual waiver applies. The KO will monitor compliance at the order level. 5. LOCAL GATE SECURITY AND CAAA DELIVERY PROTOCOLS Delivery Address: CAAA, 300 Highway 361, Crane, IN 47522. A/E Eligibility and Disciplines The selected A/E firm shall meet the FAR 2.101 definition of Architect engineer services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1102 and FAR 36.6. The SDVOSB architectural firm must employ the principal Architect responsible for the design of this project and be heavily involved in all aspects of the design, including stamping drawings along with other team disciplines. A/Es signing drawings must be licensed; licenses are required at the time of award. Project Identification Renovate Specialty Clinics on 2nd Floor Project No. 517 22 202 A/E SCOPE OF WORK GENERAL: This project, Non-recurring Maintenance, will engage an architectural/engineering (A/E) firm to provide a complete design for a new renovation of our 2nd floor specialty and support space to create updated clinic spaces. This project would provide much needed improvements at the VA Beckley Campus. This project will require extensive assistance from the A/E interior designer as this is an area that is viewed heavily by Veterans, family, visitors, and staff throughout the day to day while in the building. Our facility presently does not have an interior designer on staff. Therefore, this will require the A/E interior designer to be heavily engaged with the VA staff throughout the entire process to achieve an aesthetically pleasing appearance to the 2nd floor. Although the project is for approximately 16,530 square feet on the 2nd, an all-inclusive concept will need to be created. This will lay the groundwork to provide a world class care setting for this hospital. This project will help reinforce the quality of care that our Veterans receive. The A/E would be expected to collaborate with other A/E firms involved in other projects throughout the facility. The renovation is anticipated to be extensive due to the building s original construction dating back to the 1950 s. Given its age, significant upgrades to all systems are expected to be necessary to meet current code, standards, and VA requirements. PURPOSE: The desired result is to provide improvements for approximately 16,530 square feet of specialty clinic space, located on the 2nd floor of BECVAMC Building 1. The renovation will provide our veterans with an updated central check-in and waiting area, improved wayfinding through updated layout, and improved traffic flows. It will also improve the clinic layout as the current clinic space was originally designed for medical surgical care. The 2nd floor has approximately 58,853 square feet that must be evaluated to determine the optimum location and layout for clinic space. The existing conditions for specialty clinics are spread over many floors of the hospital with hopes to bring or relocate most/many to the 2nd floor. This project would allow our facility to utilize a one-stop care approach by bringing services directly to our Veterans in their exam rooms. By creating correctly sized exam rooms it will help to accommodate the Veterans, their family, and caregivers who accompany them to their appointments. The design would also accommodate Veterans who use mobility scooters and larger wheelchairs. Veteran privacy will be enhanced by reducing foot and equipment traffic This project will renovate to provide space to meet VA guidelines. This project would establish a central check-in and waiting area for the 2nd floor clinics that would be easily accessible and accommodate Veterans and their caregivers. The waiting area would also improve efficiency and wayfinding, as well as increase Veteran satisfaction. LOCATION: Building 1, primarily on the 2nd floor of the VA Medical Center in Beckley, WV. VA Beckley has been approved for the renovation of the 2nd floor area and support space to create, expand clinics that will comply with VA guidelines. The architect shall verify and detail all utility moves and upgrades to support the renovation floorplans. title: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1
description: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1 Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of all qualified companies; (2) whether they are small or large businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran- owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their understanding and experience relative to the proposed acquisition to assist the Government in determining the expectation of receiving bids from responsible contractors at fair market prices. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set- aside is possible. An organization that is not under the applicable NAICS code can submit a response to this notice, however their capabilities may/may not be assessed for the purposes of this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement as a set-aside based upon responses to this Notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Corps of Engineers (COE), Rock Island District does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses received. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or make a contract award. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a request for proposal, quote or invitation for bid. Interested parties are expected to review this Notice and the Project Requirements to familiarize themselves with the requirements of this project. NAICS Code and Size Standard: In the event a solicitation is issued, North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard of $45 Million, is being considered. Solicitation Type: The Government is considering using a RFO FAR 14 Invitation for Bid for solicitation of this project. Background: The Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project area spans approximately 2,350 acres along the right descending bank of the Upper Mississippi River System, situated between River Mile 327.0 to 332.0 within Pool 21. It is located in Adams County, Illinois adjacent to the City of Quincy. The project area contains several Mississippi River Project Master Plan land classifications, including Wildlife Management, High Density Recreation, and Vegetation Management land classifications. Historically, Quincy Bay was an important stopover point for diving ducks during spring and fall migrations. Sedimentation within the project area has resulted in decreased water depths and reduced habitat availability. Today, the reduced depth of the Upper Bay and lack of aquatic vegetation supports very few migratory waterfowl. Furthermore, floodplain forests have experienced an increase in invasive species and a decrease in regeneration and diversity. Relatively diverse pre-settlement floodplain forests are now largely dominated by silver maple and cottonwood. Without restoration, the project area�s open waters would continue to convert to shallow backwaters and drier bottomland forests would continue to develop into plant communities dominated by flood tolerant species and invasive species such as reed canary grass and Japanese hops. The entirety of the Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project consists of the following proposed activities and features: dredged material placement with forest rehabilitation, dredging for overwintering habitat and sediment reduction, bank stabilization, river training structures, cut-through channel modification, Cedar Creek modification, vegetated overflow structures, aquatic vegetation plantings, timber stand improvement, and pothole enhancement. The total project will be carried out in multiple stages. The focus of this Sources Sought is Stage 1: dredging for overwintering habitat, access dredging, topographic diversity enhancement, bank stabilization, and river training structures. Project Requirements: Stage 1: Dredging for Overwintering Habitat (OW 1-3), Access Dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), Topographic Diversity (TD 1-4), Bank Stabilization (BS 2), and River Training Structure (RTS 4-5) See Figure 1 for feature locations. Areas considered as part of this Project and described as the Project area include Quincy Bay, Quinsippi Island, backwater areas, and adjacent federally owned General Plan Lands. Approximately 16 acres of Quincy Bay and backwater channels will require access dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), with approximately 19 acres requiring additional dredging to create deeper overwintering habitat (OW 1-3) for native species. Mechanical excavation/dredging will be required. Channel depths are up to 8 feet below flat pool and will have a channel bottom between 50 and 60 feet wide. Quantities excavated will be approximately 260,000 cubic yards of material over a total length approaching 16,000 feet. Excavated material will be side cast where possible and shaped to tie into the existing bankline. This material will be handled multiple times. Side casting will only be possible for a portion of the material to be removed from the dredge cuts. Material that cannot be side cast and shaped will need to be hauled to the shoreline placement sites. Placement sites are located at a minimum of 25 feet from the channel cut. The placement sites vary in width ranging from approximately 40 feet wide to 60 feet wide. Material will be required to remain within the placement site limits, with no material allowed to reenter the channel cuts, or be removed from the project area. These dredge placement sites will be used for topographic diversity features (TD 1-4). A top elevation may not be exceeded at the placement sites, and material will be required to be spread evenly across the placement sites in preparation for future work. Shaping of these sites to maintain a side slope will also be required. Tree/brush clearing will be required in select locations to ensure placement sites tie into the bankline. Trees outside of the placement site limits will not be damaged or removed. Bank stabilization (BS 2) for approximately 400 linear feet on Cedar Creek will require clearing; hauling, grading, and shaping; and placement of 1,100 tons of RR3 sized stone, with approximately 8 inches of bedding stone underlay. The bank will be shaped to maintain a predetermined slope to height ratio per the project design, with consideration for the width of the stone placement. Surveying after the bank stabilization to confirm the appropriate ratio will be required. River Training Structures (RTS 4-5) along the exterior edge of topographic diversity placement (TD1) will require specific shaping of dredged material to create more diversity in the placement alignment/orientation. This will be a construction contract to be primarily constructed during 2028. Capability Statement/Information Sought: All parties interested in this project must demonstrate that they would have the potential to be a responsive and responsible contractor. Interested businesses shall include the following information to be considered for this Sources Sought announcement: Company Name, UEI/CAGE (If your company does not have at the time of this sources sought, please be aware that you will be required to register your company in the System of Award Management (SAM) system to be eligible for any future Federal contracts), POC information including an email, current small business and socio-economic status for the NAICS code listed above. title: Pre-Solicitation Notice - Trenching, Conduit and Ground-well Installation
description: Description The United Stated Embassy in Kingston, Jamaica, plans to issue a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for trenching, conduit and ground-well installation in various locations on the Embassy compound. Scope of Work: The contractor will provide all labor, equipment, supervision, material specific to the back filling and compaction and management needed to complete the job Infrastructure Support System - Handhole / Underground Conduit System Trenching Nine locations have been identified requiring trench work. Thirteen locations have been identified requiring trench work. Before excavation, the Contractor shall locate and verify all existing utilities in the proposed trench alignment. If excavation interferes with existing drains, piping, or structures, the Contractor shall immediately notify, in writing, the COR and provide temporary protection for these systems before proceeding. Trenching from Handholes The Contractor shall make wall penetrations into existing manholes/handholes as required for the number and size of conduits entering and exiting each structure, in accordance with the drawings. Conduit Existing conduit shall remain in place unless the drawings specifically direct removal or modification. Under grass, soil, the Contractor shall install Schedule 80 PVC conduit with a minimum cover of 24 inches (610 mm) from finished grade to top of conduit, or as indicated on the drawings, whichever is greater. All underground 90 degree bends with a 12inch (305 mm) radius shall use prefabricated sweeping bends. Above grade, all underground PVC conduit shall transition to rigid galvanized steel (RGS) using PVC to RGS couplers. The Contractor shall install pull lines in all new conduit runs. Soil and Backfill Materials Soil Materials The Contractor shall provide all labor and materials for soil and backfill, where required. Select Backfill: ASTM D 2487 soil classification groups SW, SP, and SM, or combinations thereof; free of rock or gravel larger than 3 inches (75 mm), debris, waste, frozen materials, vegetation, and other deleterious matter. Asphalt/Concrete Base Course: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; with at least 95% passing a 11/2inch (40 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Base Gravel: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; 100% passing a 1inch (25 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Sand Cushion: ASTM C 33 fine aggregate, natural or manufactured sand. Placement and Compaction Place backfill and fill in layers not exceeding: 8 inches (203 mm) loose thickness for heavy compaction equipment; 4 inches (102 mm) loose thickness when compacted by hand-operated tampers. Place backfill and fill evenly to the required elevations, uniformly along their full length. Compact soil materials to not less than the following percentages of maximum dry unit weight per ASTM D 1557: Under lawns or unpaved areas: scarify and re-compact top 6 inches (152 mm) below subgrade and compact each layer to 85%. Utility trenches: compact each layer of initial and final backfill to 85%. Anticipated Period of Performance: a base period of twenty-one (21) days after contract award Eligibility and Registration Offerors must hold an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) when they submit a proposal and at award. Local Insurance and Defense Based Act (DBA) Insurance. Solicitation Availability The Embassy will post the solicitation and all amendments only on SAM.gov at https://sam.gov. Interested parties should monitor SAM.gov for the release and any amendments. The Embassy will not issue paper copies. Disclaimer This notice is for informational purposes only and is not a request for proposals. It does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information or materials submitted in response to this notice. Interested Parties are required to send their interest to Kingstonquotes@state.gov on or before October 26, 2026 at 2pm local time.

title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed above. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed above. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources. Update as of 10/1/26 Submission Format Requirements Use Times New Roman, 12?point font for all text. Maintain 1?inch margins on all sides of every page. The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30?page limit. Please do not paginate these two sections. Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats. Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov. In the email subject line, format the title exactly as: �Response to GSMO?4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]� Scope Guidance NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research. If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate �Limited Scope� on the Cover Page, along with a brief description of the capabilities included. title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources. Update as of 10/1/26 Submission Format Requirements Use Times New Roman, 12?point font for all text. Maintain 1?inch margins on all sides of every page. The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30?page limit. Please do not paginate these two sections. Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats. Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov. In the email subject line, format the title exactly as: �Response to GSMO?4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]� Scope Guidance NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research. If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate �Limited Scope� on the Cover Page, along with a brief description of the capabilities included. Q&A Sessions The program intends to hold formal one?on?one Q&A sessions with vendors capable of delivering the full contract scope once the RFI period closes. Dates and duration for these sessions are TBD.

description: Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities.
